title: Route the remaining hand-literal EQS C++ defaults through eqs-defaults
body:
## Summary
Four C++ defaults the EQS views show are still string literals. They do not come from the single-source `src/lib/ai-director/eqs-defaults.ts` that both view headers say they use.

## Description
`eqs-defaults.ts` exists so one engine tweak cannot desync the views, and `src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSPipelineDiagram/types.ts` and `src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/types.ts` both claim the views 'can never silently drift'. But bPenalizeLowGround is the literal 'false' in two places (src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSPipelineDiagram/constants.ts:117, src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/eqsComponents.ts:254), and the nav projection ProjectDown=500 / ProjectUp=100 are literals in src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/constants.ts:19-20 (C++: EnvQueryGenerator_AttackPositions.cpp:13-14, EnvQueryTest_ElevationAdvantage.h:46). Fixed = add `penalizeLowGround` to EQS_ELEVATION_ADVANTAGE and a `projection` block to EQS_ATTACK_POSITIONS, then read them at every site.

## Flow
- add the fields to src/lib/ai-director/eqs-defaults.ts (outside this context's paths)
- replace the 4 literal sites
- extend the eqs-defaults parity test to pin the new fields

## Expected impact
AI designers reading the EQS views: a change to a C++ default reaches every surface. Could break: nothing visible, since the values are identical today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for every C++ default the views show
Before: 4 C++ defaults shown in the views are hand literals across 3 files (2 of them the same value duplicated)
After: 0 hand literals; all read from eqs-defaults
Method: probe - grepped the literal sites and checked them against the C++ headers; the fix needs src/lib/ai-director/eqs-defaults.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source-scan test (comments stripped): no literal default for a field eqs-defaults exports, plus the parity test extended to the 3 new fields; seed it by reintroducing a literal

title: Collapse the three EQS stage-kind color/label tables into the catalog
body:
## Summary
Three hand-maintained tables map EQS stage kind to color, and two map kind to label. The two label tables already disagree ('Score' vs 'Test (Score)').

## Description
KIND_COLORS (src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSPipelineDiagram/constants.ts:21), STEP_KIND_COLORS (src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/constants.ts:46) and KIND_META (src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/constants.ts:7) each map the same EQS kinds to the same accent tokens. The squad PipelineView labels 'test-score' as 'Score' (src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/PipelineView.tsx:17), while the diagram says 'Test (Score)' (src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSPipelineDiagram/constants.ts:158). The catalog (src/lib/ai-director/eqs-catalog.ts) already owns kind identity. Fixed = one KIND_STYLE table there, read by all three views.

## Flow
- add KIND_STYLE {color,label} to eqs-catalog.ts
- replace the 3 color tables and the 2 label tables
- test: each view renders a given kind with the catalog's label and color

## Expected impact
Designers moving between the EQS diagram and the squad pipeline see one vocabulary. Could break: badge wording in PipelineView changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one table per rule
Before: 3 color tables + 2 label tables for one kind rule; the 2 label tables disagree on 2 of 5 kinds (test-score, test-filter)
After: 1 table; 0 disagreements
Method: probe - read the 5 tables and compared entries; the shared home is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test: the same kind renders the same label and color in EQSPipelineDiagram and the squad PipelineView (red today on the label)

title: Stop announcing hovered squad members as 'selected' in a listbox with no selection
body:
## Summary
The squad member list is role=listbox, and each row's aria-selected follows hover/focus. Nothing can actually be selected, so a screen reader announces a selection model the widget does not have.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/SquadMemberRow.tsx:34 sets aria-selected={isActive}, and isActive is hover OR focus (src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/FormationView.tsx:62). Moving the pointer over a row flips its 'selected' state; activating it does nothing. Fixed = either a real single-select (click/Enter pins a member and the glyph highlight follows the pin), or a role=list of focusable items with no aria-selected.

## Flow
- hover a member row with a screen reader running -> 'selected' is announced
- press Enter -> nothing happens

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users of the squad editor. Could break: the roving-tabindex keyboard model if the role changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the announced state matches what the widget does
Before: aria-selected changes on every hover/focus event; 0 activation handlers
After: aria-selected only on a real pin (or absent)
Method: simulation - walked hover, focus and Enter on the default squad; choosing the right model needs a behaviour test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/SquadMemberRow.tsx:33-35 role="option" aria-selected={isActive}
src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/FormationView.tsx:62 const activeMember = hoveredMember ?? focusedMember
instrument: behaviour test: hovering a row leaves aria-selected unchanged; Enter pins the member, marks it selected and highlights its glyph

title: Share one ring-point generator across AttackRing and FlankAngleHeatmap
body:
## Summary
The rule that places points at even angles around a ring is written three times: twice inline in AttackRingVisualizer and once as FlankAngleHeatmap's generateRingPoints.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/index.tsx:32-44 and :46-59 are the same loop with a different radius. src/components/modules/game-systems/FlankAngleHeatmap/helpers.ts:25 is a third copy, and RingPoint is declared twice (src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/types.ts:1, src/components/modules/game-systems/FlankAngleHeatmap/helpers.ts:17). Fixed = one pure ringPoints(n, r, center) in src/components/ui/svg/polar-layout.ts (both views already use that module), with a unit test.

## Flow
- extract ringPoints into polar-layout
- replace the 3 loops
- unit-test the helper

## Expected impact
Developers: a fix to point placement lands once. Could break: FlankAngleHeatmap scoring if its start angle differs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - duplicated sites
Before: 3 copies of one ring rule, 2 RingPoint types
After: 1 implementation, 1 type
Method: probe - grepped RingPoint/generateRingPoints; FlankAngleHeatmap belongs to another context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test pinning ringPoints output for n=12 to the current AttackRing and heatmap outputs (identical before and after)

title: Replace raw rgba() literals in the attack-ring viz with theme tokens
body:
## Summary
The attack-ring visualizer hard-codes six rgba() colors instead of using chart-colors or CSS variables. The no-hex lint rule does not catch rgba, so these colors ignore the theme.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/AttackRingSvg.tsx:39,44,45 (grid and crosshair, rgba(255,255,255,...)) and :169 (badge, rgba(0,0,0,0.5)), plus the two slider gradients at src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/AttackRingControls.tsx:177,203. FormationView draws the same grid with stroke="var(--border)" (src/components/modules/game-systems/SquadChoreographyEditor/FormationView.tsx:144). Fixed = var(--border)/var(--surface-deep) with opacity, or chart-colors helpers.

## Flow
- swap the 6 literals for tokens
- check the result visually in the light and dark themes

## Expected impact
Light-theme users: today the grid is white on a light surface. Could break: the grid's contrast tuning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - colors come from tokens
Before: 6 raw rgba literals in 2 files
After: 0
Method: probe - grepped rgba( in the context; the visual result needs a human look, so it is not Lane A
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source-scan test (comments stripped) for rgba( in the context's files, plus a screenshot pair in both themes

title: Stop long UPROPERTY names overrunning the inventory description column
body:
## Summary
In the property-description list each name gets a fixed 112px column with no truncation. The longest name needs about 120px at 10px mono, so it runs into its description.

## Description
In src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/ComponentCard.tsx the description rows give the name span `shrink-0 w-28` (112px). 'NumberOfTraceHeights' is 20 chars x ~6px = ~120px, more than 112px; 'bPenalizeLowGround', 'bGenerateInnerRing' and 'CoverCheckDistance' (18 chars) come to ~108px. The table above uses a 120px grid column with `truncate` and a title. Fixed = the same column width plus truncate and title, or break-all.

## Flow
- expand Line of Sight Exposure in the inventory
- the NumberOfTraceHeights name overlaps its description

## Expected impact
Designers reading the inventory. Could break: nothing functional.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - names stay legible
Before: 1 of 23 property names is wider than its column (3 more are within 4px of the edge)
After: 0
Method: simulation - character count x 0.6em arithmetic; jsdom has no layout, so a browser screenshot is needed
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/eqsComponents.ts NumberOfTraceHeights (20 chars)
src/components/modules/game-systems/EQSComponentInventory/ComponentCard.tsx description row `text-2xs font-mono text-text-muted shrink-0 w-28`
instrument: Playwright screenshot of the expanded Line of Sight card, comparing the name span's scrollWidth with its clientWidth

title: Say that PatrolPoints' uniform-radius sampling under-fills the outer annulus
body:
## Summary
UEnvQueryGenerator_PatrolPoints picks the radius uniformly, which bunches points toward MinRadius. The app's Coverage Analysis gives only an average density and advises adding points.

## Description
The C++ (Source/PoF/AI/EQS/EnvQueryGenerator_PatrolPoints.cpp:33) and the app's mirror (src/components/modules/game-systems/PatrolPointsDistribution/helpers.ts:25) both use Radius = FRandRange(MinR, MaxR); spreading points evenly over the area needs a square-root draw. With the 500-1500 defaults, the radius that splits the area in half is sqrt((500^2+1500^2)/2) = 1118, so P(r > 1118) = 38.2%: the outer half of the patrol area gets 38% of the points and the inner half 62%. src/components/modules/game-systems/PatrolPointsDistribution/index.tsx:270-283 reports 'average density' as if the spread were even. The options: fix the generator (square-root draw in the C++ and the mirror), which changes gameplay in the UE tree, or state the bias in the copy.

## Flow
- decide: change the engine generator (UE repo, owner's call) or document the bias
- if the engine changes: square-root draw in the C++ + the mirror + a re-pin of tactical-viz-rng

## Expected impact
AI designers tuning patrol coverage: NPCs patrol the inner half about 1.6x as densely. Could break: the existing patrol feel in levels.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the coverage claim matches the sampler
Before: the outer 50% of the area gets 38.2% of the points (analytic, defaults 500/1500)
After: 50% with a square-root draw, or copy that states 38/62
Method: simulation - analytic CDF of the uniform-radius sampler at the shipped defaults; the engine change lives in another repository
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
Source/PoF/AI/EQS/EnvQueryGenerator_PatrolPoints.cpp:33 const float Radius = FMath::FRandRange(MinR, MaxR);
src/components/modules/game-systems/PatrolPointsDistribution/helpers.ts:25 const radius = minR + rng() * (maxR - minR);

title: Show that the attack-ring slider stops at 500 though the engine has no ClampMax
body:
## Summary
The AttackDistance slider stops at 500 and prints '500' as its end label. UEnvQueryGenerator_AttackPositions declares only ClampMin=50, so the cap is a drawing limit that reads like an engine bound.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/constants.ts:16 sets MAX_DISTANCE = 500 so the ring fits the viewBox. The slider prints it as its right-hand label next to 'ClampMin=50' (src/components/modules/game-systems/AttackRingVisualizer/AttackRingControls.tsx:206-209), but the C++ header has only `meta = (ClampMin = "50")`. Fixed = label the cap as a preview limit ('preview max 500'), or scale the SVG to the value.

## Flow
- open the attack ring viz
- the distance range reads 50 ... ClampMin=50 ... 500

## Expected impact
Designers reading engine bounds off the viz. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the copy tells engine bounds apart from preview limits
Before: 1 of the 3 printed bounds has no C++ source
After: 0 unsourced bounds
Method: probe - compared the printed bounds with the C++ meta
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test: the slider's max label says 'preview' while MAX_DISTANCE is not a C++ clamp
